question: how far off is the absolute 3D hand position and depth of the existing pipeline when the camera focal length is wrong

data_selection.rgb_filter: camera must have the RGB segment matching the annotation (gigahands_demo_camera_benchmark_v1.usable_for_camera_benchmark)
data_selection.sampling_rule: group by (sequence, camera); shuffle groups with the seed; take frames round-robin across groups, evenly spaced in time within a group

PIPELINE_BASELINE_FOCAL.kind: training-convention virtual focal, in original image pixels

GT_EFFECTIVE_FOCAL.why: the pipeline focal is already in original full-image pixels and there is no image resize, so no conversion is required; derived in focal_usage_audit.md section 4
GT_EFFECTIVE_FOCAL.scalar_choice: fx is used because the pipeline takes a single scalar; fy differs by 0.1-0.3 % and both are stored per row

recomputed_per_condition: camera translation tz (the only focal-dependent term)

hand_association_rule.signal: 2D only: predicted keypoint centroid vs provided 2D annotation centroid
hand_association_rule.never_uses: 3D error (that would select the quantity under study)
hand_association_rule.on_failure: record AMBIGUOUS_HAND_ASSOCIATION and drop the frame

reference_3d.transform: world -> camera with the CAM-EXP-001 validated R, t

principal_point: not swept: the pipeline uses the image centre and never reads the calibrated cx, cy, so it is structurally insensitive to it (focal_usage_audit.md section 6)

metric_families.ABSOLUTE_ERROR: prediction vs provided 3D; contains hand-model, detector and weak-perspective error as well as focal error
metric_families.INCREMENTAL_FOCAL_EFFECT: prediction at alpha vs prediction at alpha = 1.0; isolates the focal exactly
